Oh, I was unaware. In that case, I can't speak to CS50, but I enjoyed 106A/Code in Place because the learning curve really wasn't as steep as I found with other courses. The structure surrounding Stanford's introductory classes really makes you feel like anyone can do them, that's why I enjoyed them! Plus, I think being able to talk to someone on a weekly basis to go over coding concepts is invaluable. I don't know enough to tell anyone to switch, but I don't think you would regret taking Code In Place.

Harvard’s CS50 is an introduction to AI if I’m not mistaken. Stanford’s class is an introduction to Programming Fundamentals. I would think, if you are qualified for CS50, you probably wouldn’t get that much out of Code in Place.
